result.summary: Mask sensitive configuration options loaded from `settings.json` when logging startup arguments in `ArgsManager::LogArgs`. Keys in `m_settings.rw_settings` are parsed with `InterpretKey` to look up their argument flags and replace their logged value with `****` if flagged `SENSITIVE`.
result.problem: Sensitive settings such as `rpcpassword`, `rpcauth`, or `torpassword` provided via command-line arguments or `bitcoin.conf` are masked when logged, but options read from `settings.json` (`rw_settings`) are printed in cleartext to `debug.log` and stdout during node initialization.
evidence: "`ArgsManager::LogArgs` masks `SENSITIVE` options from `bitcoin.conf` and the command line via `logArgsPrefix`, but prints `m_settings.rw_settings` values verbatim. Secrets such as `rpcpassword`, `rpcuser`, `rpcauth`, or `torpassword` stored in `settings.json` are therefore written in cleartext to `debug.log` and startup console output." (PR description)
Diff in `src/common/args.cpp` directly confirms `m_settings.rw_settings` previously logged `setting.second.write()` with no flag checks, now checks `*flags & SENSITIVE`.
result.changed_since_previous: Diff and tests are now provided (the previous description had no patch). The core logic remains identical, adding unit and functional test coverage in `src/test/getarg_tests.cpp` and `test/functional/feature_settings.py`.
result.card: Mask sensitive configuration values stored in settings.json when logged by ArgsManager::LogArgs at startup. Currently, secrets like rpcpassword, rpcauth, or torpassword are masked when provided via configuration files or the command line but leaked in cleartext to debug.log and the console if stored in settings.json. The fix resolves setting keys to their registered flags and replaces sensitive values with asterisks, preventing credential leaks in logs.

risk.why: Only alters log formatting of settings at startup; worst case is incorrect masking or formatting in debug.log.
